meta.name: SGLang vs vLLM on replayed agent traffic
meta.question: At equal hardware and identical agent traffic, does the serving engine (stock vLLM vs SGLang) change throughput and latency for this hybrid-attention model?

traffic.source: Recorded mini-swe-agent sessions from our own Terminal-Bench 2.0 runs at 32 agents with vLLM defaults

replay: None executed: each request re-sends the conversation exactly as the agent sent it before its i-th reply, with the bash tool schema, and asks for exactly as many tokens as the recorded reply (ignore_eos, temperature 0.6, streaming).

metrics.name: requests_completed
metrics.definition: requests that returned without error and with a usage block within the run.

metrics.name: generated_tokens_per_s
metrics.definition: completion tokens of completed requests / measured_window_s (the actual replay duration, which runs past 720 s while in-flight requests finish).

metrics.name: request_latency_p50_s / p90_s
metrics.definition: median / 90th percentile of request wall time over completed requests.

metrics.name: ttft_p50_s
metrics.definition: median time to the first streamed chunk.

metrics.name: running_requests_peak
metrics.definition: peak of the engine's running-requests gauge, scraped every 10 s.

failure.definition: Request failed with a connection reset from the server.
failure.example: A streamed request was reset by the SGLang server while the radix cache was off.

limitations: One run per setting; no repeats or confidence intervals.
One model (a hybrid Gated DeltaNet + attention model, where SGLang's per-request linear-attention state is the bottleneck), one GPU type (H100), one workload (mini-swe-agent traffic at 32 sessions).
Only two non-default SGLang settings were tried, following its cookbook; not an exhaustive tuning of either engine.
Measures serving throughput and latency only, not agent outcomes.
Replay re-sends recorded prompts with fixed generation lengths (ignore_eos); real agents would react to slower responses (fewer turns per time limit).
Runs reached different numbers of sessions (39-55 of 124) within the window, so later sessions with longer prompts are weighted differently across engines.
Replayed prompts were a median 0.8769-0.9256 of the recorded prompt token counts (reasoning text is not re-sent), so prefix sharing is close to but not identical with the original run.
